executiveSummary: Available reporting indicates the UK Maritime and Coastguard Agency (MCA) published MGN 719 (M+F), advising maritime stakeholders to prepare for GNSS-denied and degraded environments, including potential jamming and spoofing that could disrupt navigation, tracking, VTS, and port operations. Government Advisory Current reporting suggests operational dependencies on GNSS for position, velocity, timing (PVT), and network time synchronization create cross-domain risks spanning bridge systems (ECDIS, AIS, radar overlays), dynamic positioning, and port/terminal systems reliant on precise time. The collected intelligence supports an assessment that immediate defensive attention should prioritize navigation resilience measures: contingency procedures, cross-checking with alternative navigation sources, crew training, and dependency mapping across shipboard and shore-based systems. Confidence: high, based on government guidance. Source No active cyber incidents, malware campaigns, or vendor-specific vulnerabilities are identified in the supplied reporting set. Accordingly, the overall maritime cyber threat level is assessed as MODERATE for this period due to credible navigation exposure rather than active exploitation. Outlook judgment: In the next 72 hours, operators should prioritize awareness and drills for GNSS anomalies and ensure bridge teams can transition to alternative methods if required. Confidence: medium (analytical synthesis anchored to the MCA advisory). Supporting Report

Vendors: Not specified in source reporting.

keyFindings: MGN 719 (M+F) highlights risks from GNSS denial, degradation, jamming, and spoofing across shipboard and shore-based systems, advising contingency planning and training.
Operational exposure includes navigation continuity, VTS awareness, and time-dependent port and logistics functions.

events.title: UK MCA issues GNSS-denied/degraded operations guidance (MGN 719)
events.text: Publication: 2026-10-01 • Source: GOV.UK (Government) Intelligence: Official guidance flags risks from GNSS denial, degradation, jamming, and spoofing; calls for contingency planning, alternative navigation, training, and dependency assessment. Maritime domains: Navigation, Ports, VTS (per advisory scope). Affected systems: GNSS receivers, ECDIS, AIS, DP, integrated bridge systems, VTS tracking, and GNSS-timed IT/OT. Operational impact: Possible degradation of navigation continuity and situational awareness; potential timing drifts impacting port/logistics operations. Navigation impact: Possible (false/faulty position, timing errors). Safety impact: Possible (increased collision/grounding risk if unmitigated). Supply-chain impact: Possible (ETA reliability, queuing, scheduling). TTPs observed: GNSS jamming and spoofing described at a conceptual level (no actor attribution provided). Mitigations: Contingency procedures, alternative navigation, training, and dependency mapping as directed in the advisory.
